findings.description: Every RateLimitError terminates an unverified invocation, including ordinary requests-per-minute limits. The supplied request-rate test explicitly requires these errors to walk the chain.
findings.failure_mode: A request-rate 429 prevents an available fallback from serving the request and incorrectly reports that calibration is needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the error's token_limited flag before taking the RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED exit; preserve normal fallback handling for request-rate limits.

findings.description: _ceiling_unverified is calculated for the preflight head and reused for every fallback, although each hop has its own probed and calibrated bounds.
findings.failure_mode: After an unverified head fails, a calibrated fallback's token-limit 429 incorrectly terminates the chain and writes an unverified calibration record. Conversely, a fallback running above its own probed bound can retain the head's verified status.
findings.suggested_fix: Recompute unverified status against the current hop's catalog entry, effective input count, and ceiling policy before dispatch.

findings.description: The premium threshold checks only input_tokens. Anthropic cache-read and cache-creation tokens are separate from input_tokens, as documented by create_ledger_entry, but contribute to the request's input size.
findings.failure_mode: A request with 150,000 uncached input tokens and 100,000 cached tokens misses the 200,000-token premium threshold, underreporting both input-side and output-side costs.
findings.suggested_fix: Determine premium eligibility using input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens, then apply the multipliers to all applicable cost components.

findings.description: The context-budget shrink uses continue inside the existing bounded retry loop without reserving another attempt.
findings.failure_mode: When a shrinkable context error occurs on the final permitted attempt, including the first attempt with max_retries=0, the request is replaced but never dispatched again. Execution falls through to retry exhaustion instead of performing the promised single shrink retry.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the context-shrink retry its own one-shot allowance while retaining the global attempt-budget check, or explicitly handle exhaustion before consuming the context error.

findings.description: The new calibration exit stores str(_exc) as message_redacted and interpolates the same unredacted provider message into stderr JSON.
findings.failure_mode: A provider error containing an echoed credential is exposed in operator logs and passed into models_failed without redaction. The supplied calibration-redaction test exercises this exact case.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the existing secret-redaction helper to the provider message before recording it or printing it, and reuse the sanitized message for both outputs.

findings.description: `_ceiling_unverified` is computed once from the HEAD entry's pre-flight GateOutcome and is never re-evaluated per hop, yet it drives two terminal, non-walkable exits inside the chain loop: the `RateLimitError` short-circuit (line 2297) and the error_class choice for `ProviderContextLimitError` (line 2256). In addition, the `RateLimitError` arm fires on ANY 429 while the flag is set; it does not distinguish a token-limit 429 from a plain request-rate 429. The PR's own tests encode the opposite contract: `test_request_rate_429_while_unverified_walks_to_the_next_hop` (BB-003) expects a plain `RateLimitError` to walk with no calibration row, and `test_unverified_status_is_per_hop_not_inherited_from_the_head` (DISS-001) expects a 429 / provider limit on a CALIBRATED fallback hop to be classed PROVIDER_OUTAGE / PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT. Those tests also construct `RateLimitError("anthropic", token_limited=True)`, a kwarg the types.py hunk in this diff does not add, so the diff as shown cannot pass them.
findings.failure_mode: Under LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived, an ordinary requests-per-minute 429 on the head (after transport backoff) ends the invocation with exit RATE_LIMITED instead of walking to the operator's declared fallback, and appends a RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED row to `.run/ceiling-observed.json` that attributes a rate-limit to the ceiling. A 429 or provider size verdict on a later, calibrated hop is likewise mislabeled as unverified and short-circuits the chain. The declared chain shape (the operator's contract) is silently not honored.
findings.suggested_fix: Track unverified status per hop: compute it from `input_bound(_hop_entry, ...)` / the hop's own gate decision inside the loop (or reset `_ceiling_unverified` to False for every entry after the head and set it only when that hop dispatches above its probed bound). Gate the RateLimitError short-circuit on a token-limit signal (`getattr(_e, 'token_limited', False)`) and add that field to `RateLimitError` in types.py, populated by the adapters from the 429 body (`input tokens per minute` class). Keep request-rate 429s on the existing walk path.

findings.description: The one-shot output-budget shrink does `continue` without checking whether another attempt remains. When `ProviderContextLimitError` arrives on the final iteration (max_retries == 0, or the earlier attempts were consumed by 429/5xx), the loop simply ends and whatever follows the loop raises (presumably `RetriesExhaustedError`) with `last_typed_error` still None, because this arm never sets it.
findings.failure_mode: The provider's size verdict is re-typed as a generic retries-exhausted failure. In cheval.py that path is walkable, so the fallback hop receives the same oversized payload (the exact thing D-1.1b says must never happen), no observed-bound record is written, and the `calibration_needed` envelope is absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Before `continue`, check `attempt < max_retries` (and the global attempt budget); if no attempt remains, `raise` the original error. Also set `last_typed_error = e` in this arm so any exhaustion path carries the typed cause.

findings.description: The long-context tier triggers on `input_tokens > threshold` only. For Anthropic usage, `input_tokens` excludes `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` (ledger.py docstring: 'not part of input_tokens'), while the provider's published 1M-window rule applies the premium when the request's TOTAL input (including cached prompt tokens) exceeds 200K. The multipliers are then applied to the cache costs, so the code clearly intends cache traffic to be part of the premium, but it is not part of the trigger.
findings.failure_mode: A request of 60K fresh input + 150K cache-read tokens (210K billed input) is ledgered at base rates while the provider bills the 2.0x/1.5x tier; `long_context: false`, under-reporting spend and breaking the cost-report `long_context_rows` count.
findings.suggested_fix: Trigger on `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens > threshold` (and document the choice next to the `verified: False` flag in the catalog block). Add a unit test with cache tokens straddling the threshold.

findings.description: `_calibration_needed_exit` writes `"message_redacted": str(_exc)` into `models_failed` and interpolates `f"{_exc} — ..."` into the stderr `_error_json`, with no redaction call. The exception message is the provider's raw HTTP error body (`f"HTTP {status} context-limit: {_msg}"`). The head test `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` patches `redact_payload_strings` to identity and still expects the key to be absent, which only holds if `ChevalError.__init__` or `_error_json` redacts. Nothing in this diff does.
findings.failure_mode: If no upstream redaction exists, a secret-shaped fragment echoed in a provider error body lands verbatim in the MODELINV envelope and operator stderr log.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the message through the existing redaction helper (the one the other `models_failed` arms use) before storing or printing it, matching the `message_redacted` field name's contract.

findings.cross_file_justification: The match predicate `is_context_limit_message` lives in routing/ceiling.py (truncated from this review); the consequence of a false positive is a non-walkable exit plus a persisted bound-lowering record in cheval.py's `_calibration_needed_exit`.
findings.description: Every HTTP 400 is first tested with `is_context_limit_message` and, on match, raised as the non-walkable `ProviderContextLimitError` ahead of the billing-class check. Anthropic also returns 400s of the shape `max_tokens: 128000 > 64000, which is the maximum allowed number of output tokens` and `thinking.budget_tokens ... exceeds max_tokens`. If the predicate keys on generic words ('exceed', 'maximum', 'too long') these output-side errors are misclassified. `parse_context_limit` would then yield no `input_tokens`, so `_calibration_needed_exit` falls back to `_obs = _walk_estimate` and records it as an observed input bound.
findings.failure_mode: An output-budget misconfiguration becomes a permanent (until calibration) lowering of the entry's input ceiling in `.run/ceiling-observed.json`, and the chain is not walked even though a fallback hop with a smaller max_output_tokens would have succeeded.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the predicate anchor on the provider's actual prompt-size phrasings (`prompt is too long`, `input length and max_tokens exceed context limit`, HTTP 413) and explicitly exclude `max_tokens:`-prefixed messages. In `_calibration_needed_exit`, do not lower the bound when the provider supplied neither `input_tokens` nor `limit`.

findings.description: `_CONTEXT_FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS = 4_096` duplicates `routing.ceiling.FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS` as a literal with a comment promising equality. Nothing enforces it. This is exactly the class of 'size decision outside the catalog policy' the sprint sets out to remove: if the floor is tuned in ceiling.py (or made catalog-driven), the retry layer's shrink keeps the stale literal and will either refuse a shrink the gate would accept or retry at a budget the gate considers unusable.
findings.failure_mode: Silent drift between the gate's floor and the retry layer's floor after any future change; no test fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test asserting `retry._CONTEXT_FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS == ceiling.FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS`, or move the constant into `loa_cheval.types` (already imported by both) so there is one definition.
